newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Bohai region to become shipping base.
newsitem.headline: China's Bohai region to become shipping base.

text.p: China's northeastern Bohai region is expected to show rapid economic growth and become the largest container shipping centre in northern China in the next century, the China Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The shipping centre along the Bohai Bay would be framed by China's top container ports of Dalian, Tianjin and Qingdao, and the ports of Yantai and Qinghuangdao, it said.
Dalian was currently building the first phase of the Dayaowan deep-water wharves, consisting of 10 docks including two 30,000-tonne container docks and two 25,000-tonne multi-function docks, it said.
The second phase would add another 10 docks and the Dayaowan Port would be able to handle 60 million tonnes of cargo annually on completion in three years, it said.
The capacity of Qingdao and Tianjin ports had also grown, it said but gave no further details.

By 2000, the region's ports would handle an annual 3.3-3.7 million Twenty-Foot Equivalent Units (TEU) of containers. In 10 years, the ports would be able to handle another 14 million TEUs, it said without elaborating.
Growth in handling capacity of ports in northern China had lagged behind the national level and that suggested there was still potential for development, it said.
The region had abundant labour resources and was a favourite destination for Japanese and South Korean investment, it said.
The Bohai region, extending across northeastern Liaoning, Hebei and Shandong provinces and including the cities of Beijing and Tianjin, is a base for heavy industry and machinery manufacturing.
